concepts.name: Asexual Reproduction
concepts.description: Learners should understand that asexual reproduction produces offspring with very few differences due to minor DNA copying errors.
concepts.evidence: In asexual reproduction, such as in bacteria, very few differences appear between generations because they arise only from small inaccuracies in DNA copying.

concepts.name: Sexual Reproduction
concepts.description: Learners should know that sexual reproduction creates greater genetic diversity because offspring receive DNA from two parents.
concepts.evidence: In sexual reproduction, even greater diversity is generated, because each offspring receives DNA from two parents.

concepts.name: Genetic Variation
concepts.description: Learners should recognize that variation among individuals increases a species' chances of survival in changing environments.
concepts.evidence: Variations accumulate across generations, and the great advantage of variation to a species is that it increases the chances of survival in a changing environment.

concepts.name: Dominant & Recessive Traits
concepts.description: Learners should be able to identify which trait is expressed (dominant) and which is hidden (recessive) in a heterozygote.
concepts.evidence: The trait that is expressed is called dominant, and the trait that is not expressed is called recessive.

concepts.name: Monohybrid Ratio
concepts.description: Learners should calculate the 3:1 phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation of a monohybrid cross.
concepts.evidence: In the F2 generation, tall and short plants appeared in a ratio of about 3:1.

concepts.name: Independent Assortment
concepts.description: Learners should understand that different gene pairs segregate independently during gamete formation, producing new trait combinations.
concepts.evidence: This showed that the tall/short trait and the round/wrinkled seed trait are inherited independently of each other.

concepts.name: Dihybrid Ratio
concepts.description: Learners should predict the 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio resulting from a dihybrid cross.
concepts.evidence: In such a dihybrid cross the four combinations appear in the ratio 9:3:3:1.

concepts.name: Gene Definition
concepts.description: Learners should know that a gene is a DNA segment that provides the information for making a specific protein.
concepts.evidence: Cellular DNA is the information source for making proteins in the cell. A section of DNA that provides information for one protein is called the gene for that protein.

concepts.name: Sex Determination
concepts.description: Learners should explain how sex chromosomes (XX or XY) determine the sex of human offspring.
concepts.evidence: Women have a perfect pair, both called X, while men have a mismatched pair, one normal-sized X and one short chromosome called Y.

concepts.name: Chromosome Number Restoration
concepts.description: Learners should understand that fertilisation restores the normal diploid chromosome number by combining one set from each parent.
concepts.evidence: when two germ cells combine, the normal number of chromosomes, with one copy from each parent, is restored.
